title: How Much Effort Does an AI Code Reviewer Need? Evidence from Claude 5.5 Models on Plausible-but-Wrong Patches
abstract: arXiv:2611.33639v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI coding agents write code faster than people can review it, so teams add AI reviewers. Reasoning models let such a reviewer trade cost for diligence through an effort setting. We asked how much effort a reviewer needs to catch plausible-but-wrong patches, which pass a benchmark's tests but fail stronger ones. Claude Opus 5.5 (preregistered), Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 (exploratory) each reviewed the same 90 agent-written Django patches from SWE-bench Verified at low, medium and high effort. By strengthened SWE-ABS tests, 55 patches were wrong and 35 correct. In every model, high effort accepted fewer wrong patches than low (false success .45 against .67 for Opus, .49 against .65 for Sonnet, .51 against .78 for Haiku), a supported difference for Opus and Haiku. For Opus, medium was non-inferior to high within 15 percentage points (difference .018, 95% CI [-.065, .108]) and cost 20% less, short of the preregistered 30%. For Sonnet and Haik

translated_title: AI代码审查者需要多少努力程度？来自Claude 5.5模型对似是而非错误补丁的证据
translated_abstract: AI编码代理编写代码的速度超过了人类审查代码的速度，因此团队开始引入AI审查者。推理模型使这样的审查者能够通过努力程度设置在成本与细致程度之间进行权衡。我们探究了审查者需要多少努力才能发现似是而非的错误补丁——即能通过基准测试但在更强测试下失败的补丁。Claude Opus 5.5（预注册）、Sonnet 5.5和Haiku 5.5（探索性）各自以低、中、高三档努力程度审查了相同的90个来自SWE-bench Verified的代理编写的Django补丁。通过强化后的SWE-ABS测试，其中55个补丁是错误的，35个是正确的。在所有模型中，高等努力程度比低等努力程度接受更少的错误补丁（Opus的虚假成功率为0.45对0.67，Sonnet为0.49对0.65，Haiku为0.51对0.78），其中Opus和Haiku的差异得到统计学支持。对于Opus，中等努力程度在15个百分点范围内不劣于高等努力程度（差异0.018，95% CI [-.065, .108]），且成本降低20%，未达到预注册的30%标准。对于Sonnet和Haiku……
tldr: 通过对Claude 5.5系列模型审查90个SWE-bench补丁的预注册实验，本研究发现更高的推理努力程度能显著减少AI代码审查者对似是而非错误补丁的误接受，且对Opus而言中等努力程度能以低20%的成本达到与高等努力程度相当的效果。
en_tdlr: Through preregistered experiments with Claude 5.5 models reviewing 90 SWE-bench patches, higher reasoning effort significantly reduces AI code reviewers' false acceptance of plausible-but-wrong patches, and for Opus, medium effort achieves non-inferior performance to high effort at 20% lower cost.
